description: Core data model: Phase entity — an ordered column within a Pipe's Kanban board, holding a set of Fields
ui_details: Confirmed: Gerenciar (pipe settings dropdown) > Fases opens a full-screen editor at /pipes/:id/settings/phases. Top-left is a phase switcher dropdown (phase names, clicking one navs to /settings/phases/:phaseId) + '+ Criar uma nova fase'. Top-right has 'Condicionais em campos' and 'Opções Avançadas' buttons (see feature-003/feature-009). Left rail is the field-type palette; center is the live phase form editor (drag-and-drop or click-to-add); phases already marked done show an 'Esta é uma fase final' badge above the phase name in the center panel.
behavior: A Phase has id, name, done (boolean, marks terminal phase), cards_count, and an ordered list of Fields. Phases belong to exactly one Pipe and are ordered left-to-right on the board. Confirmed in UI (Gerenciar > Fases > Opções Avançadas modal, per-phase): editable name + color swatch, description text (shown to users working the pipe), 'Definir como fase final de processo' checkbox = the done flag (when checked, the phase view shows an 'Esta é uma fase final' badge), 'Permitir criar cards nesta fase' checkbox (lets cards be created directly into a non-initial phase), 'Gerenciar tarefas' radio (Coletar endereços de e-mail / Não coletar — task email-collection setting), 'Adicionar responsável' (auto-assign one or more members to cards entering this phase), 'Alerta de atraso' SLA (Tempo + Unidade fields — numeric duration + unit, e.g. hours/days, before a card is flagged late in this phase), and 'Excluir esta fase' (destructive, irreversible per the UI's own warning text).
data_model: phases: id, pipe_id (fk), name, position (int), done (bool), color, description (text), allow_card_creation (bool), sla_time (int, nullable), sla_unit (enum: hours|days, nullable), auto_assign_user_ids (jsonb array), collect_task_emails (bool)

description: Core data model: Field type system (23 types) shared across phase fields, start form fields, and table fields
ui_details: Confirmed: in Gerenciar > Fases, each field-type button in the left palette opens a config modal (Título do campo input, 'Escolha o tipo' dropdown that only swaps within the same conversion family — e.g. Texto curto<->Texto longo used internal values 'ShortText'/'LongText' [PascalCase, differs from the snake_case type names in the public GraphQL docs], Checklist vertical<->Checklist horizontal — confirming type conversion is restricted to compatible types, not any-to-any), toggles for Descrição, Texto de ajuda, 'Este campo é obrigatório', 'Validação customizada', 'Visualização compacta' (= minimal_view), 'Este campo é editável em outras fases' (on by default), 'Este campo deve ter valor único', plus a live right-hand preview pane that updates as you type/toggle. Choice-type fields (Checklist, and by extension Select/Radio/Label) add an 'Adicione as opções' section: a numbered list of option text inputs each with a delete (trash) icon, 'Adicionar opção +' to append one row, and 'Adicionar vários' for bulk paste. The Responsável (assignee_select) field's modal swaps 'Validação customizada'/'valor único' for a 'Sincronizar campos do card com este campo fixo' toggle instead. Anexo (attachment) shows an '+ Upload file' control in its preview. Saving shows a toast 'Configurações atualizadas.' and the field appears in the center form with hover-revealed icons: an AI-suggestion sparkle, an edit pencil, and a kebab '...' menu.
behavior: A Field has id (slug auto-generated from label), label, type, required, help, description, editable, minimal_view, and options (for choice types). Field types: assignee_select, attachment, checklist_horizontal, checklist_vertical, cnpj, connector, cpf, currency, date, datetime, due_date, email, id, label_select, long_text, number, phone, radio_horizontal, radio_vertical, select, short_text, statement, time. connector fields reference another pipe or table via connectedRepoId.
data_model: fields: id (slug, unique per phase/table), owner_type (phase|start_form|table), owner_id (fk), label, type (enum), required (bool), help (text), description (text), editable (bool), minimal_view (bool), options (jsonb array), connector_target_id (fk, nullable)

description: Core data model: Card entity — the unit of work moving through a Pipe's phases, holding Card Field Values
ui_details: Confirmed (Iteration 3, live test): Kanban 'Criar novo card' / a phase column's '+' is BLOCKED until the pipe's start form has ≥1 field — with an empty start form both open a 'Compartilhar formulário' promo modal instead of a create form. Once the start form has a field, the same buttons open an inline popover create-form (title + fields + 'Criar novo card' submit); required-field validation shows a red border + 'deve ser informado' inline, no toast, submit blocked. On success: toast 'Card criado com sucesso. Para abri-lo, clique aqui' + card appears at top of its phase column titled with the first field's submitted value. Card detail view (3 columns): LEFT = title, quick actions (Adicionar responsável/Vencimento/Adicionar etiquetas), tab strip (Form/Atividades/Anexos/Checklists/Comentários/Email/PDF/+), read-only 'Formulário Inicial' section (creator + relative timestamp + submitted field values), 'Histórico' phase-transition timeline, 'Editar visualização do card' link. MIDDLE = 'Fase atual' badge + gear (phase settings) + Compartilhar, then the current phase's own fields as a live autosave-on-blur form (no save button; no toast on this particular autosave). RIGHT = 'Mover card para fase' one-click button naming the next phase, 'Configurar mover cards', 'Mover cards com IA'. Cards in a done:true phase render a checkmark + '<N>min' badge and dimmed title text.
behavior: A Card has id, title, done (bool), updated_at, belongs to a current phase, and has many field values ({name, value, filled_at, field}). Cards move between phases (drag-and-drop on Kanban, or the detail view's quick-mover button); moving a card fires toast 'Card movido com sucesso para <Fase>. Para reabri-lo, clique aqui' and appends a Histórico entry. Card title is set once at creation from the FIRST field's submitted value on the start form and does not re-derive later. CONFIRMED: a start-form field and a phase field with the identical label are separate Field rows with independent values — the clone must not merge/dedupe fields by label across owner types (start_form vs phase). Confirmed non-cloneable client quirk: phase column card-count badges do not live-update after a same-session move — only correct after a full reload; the clone should update counts synchronously instead.
data_model: cards: id, pipe_id (fk), phase_id (fk), title, done (bool), created_at, updated_at. card_field_values: id, card_id (fk), field_id (fk), value (text), filled_at

description: Database Table entity — spreadsheet-like structured data object, separate from Pipes, with its own fields and records
page: Início > Databases tab (list) / /apollo_databases/:id (grid) / /apollo_databases/:id/records/:recordId (record detail) / /apollo_databases/:id/settings/general-settings (Configurações de database)
ui_details: Confirmed (Iteration 4, live test): 'Criar database' is a name-only modal, lands on an empty grid ('Título' column + 'Criar registro' FAB). Grid column '+' opens the same field-config modal shape as the Fases editor (Título do campo, Escolha o tipo, toggles, live preview, 'Dependências do campo' link) with a fuller palette than phases: Responsável, Anexo, Texto curto, Checkbox, Documentos, Moeda (nested currency-code sub-type e.g. 'USD - US Dollar'), Data, Data e hora, Data de vencimento, Email, ID, Etiquetas, Texto longo, Numérico, Número de telefone, Seleção de única opção, Seleção de lista, Texto fixo, Tempo, plus a 'Campos de conexão' group with only 'Conexão de database' (narrower than phase connectors, which can also target a pipe). The Formulário inicial settings tab additionally lists 'Conteúdo dinâmico' — a field type not seen in the Fases editor, not yet tested. 'Dependências do campo' is a read-only impact-analysis viewer ('Nenhuma dependência encontrada' + note that apps/integrations aren't listed), NOT a rule editor — unrelated to feature-009's Field Conditionals. Record creation modal lists only non-title fields (no separate Título input, unlike Cards); currency fields auto-mask raw digit input as cents ('15000' -> '$ 150.00' live). Record detail opens as a deep-linkable modal (icon+title, status badge w/ dropdown, 'Informações de registro' creator/timestamp, per-field hover-'Editar' inline edit w/ Salvar/Cancelar, 'Atualizado em' footer, '⋮' kebab with 'Editar campos'/'Deletar registro'). Configurações de database (Gerenciar) has: 'Título do registro' (dropdown choosing which field is the record's display title), 'Subtítulo do registro conectado' (default 'Criado em'), 'Texto do botão de criar registros' (default 'Criar registro'), 'Permissões' (Database público/privado radio), 'Autorizações' (checkbox: all members can create/edit/delete records), 'Excluir database'. Screenshots: screenshots/inspect/database-grid.jpg, screenshots/inspect/database-record-detail.jpg.
behavior: A Table has id (alphanumeric), name, public (bool), and table_fields (same type system as phase fields, richer palette per ui_details). A Table Record has id, title, and record_fields with rich per-type value columns (date_value, datetime_value, float_value, native_value, report_value). CONFIRMED: record title is NOT hardcoded to 'first field' — it's driven by an explicit title_field_id configured in Configurações de database, a real schema difference from Cards (whose title comes from the start form's first field and never re-derives). CONFIRMED client staleness quirk, same family as feature-004's Kanban count bug: saving a new field via '+' does not render the new column until reload (confirmed the save DID succeed server-side via a subsequent 'já está em uso' validation error on the label); a newly created record's own field values render as 'Vazio' and the 'N registros' header count doesn't update until reload either. CONFIRMED target-app bug (do not reproduce): the record detail modal's title-row status badge does not refresh after an inline field edit, persisting even across a fresh page navigation, while the field's own value and the grid row are both correct.
data_model: tables: id, org_id (fk), name, public (bool), title_field_id (fk, nullable), subtitle_template (text, default 'Criado em'), create_button_label (text, default 'Criar registro'), all_members_can_crud (bool). table_records: id, table_id (fk), title (derived live from title_field_id's value), created_at, updated_at. table_record_field_values: id, record_id (fk), field_id (fk), value (text), date_value, datetime_value, float_value

description: Webhook registration and outbound event delivery for pipe/table events
ui_details: TBD — not yet observed as a standalone webhook-management UI. Confirmed (iteration 5): outbound HTTP is exposed to end users as an Automations action ('Faça uma requisição HTTP') and a matching trigger ('Uma resposta for recebida da automação de requisição HTTP') — see feature-010. Pipefy does not appear to have a separate generic webhook-registration settings page distinct from the Automations builder; model outbound events as the Automations HTTP action/trigger pair, not a separate subscription list.
behavior: Org/pipe/table-scoped webhook URLs receive an HTTP POST when relevant events occur (card created/moved/updated, table record created/updated). Mirrors organization-webhooks.md and pipe-table-webhooks.md event shapes. In the live product this is implemented via the Automations engine's 'Faça uma requisição HTTP' action (any trigger → outbound POST) and its paired 'response received' trigger (an HTTP call-and-continue pattern, letting a follow-up automation act on the response body) rather than a persistent webhook-subscription CRUD screen.

description: Automations engine: pipe-scoped trigger→action rules (10 trigger types × 12 action types), with a token/variable picker for dynamic values
ui_details: Confirmed (iteration 5, live test, created + fired a real rule): list view has search, Filtros, 'Ordenar por', a per-row on/off toggle, and a kebab (Editar/Duplicar/Excluir); empty state shows a two-icon diagram + 'Nova automação' CTA. The builder is a two-column 'Sempre que... / Faça isso...' picker. Triggers: 'Um card entrar em uma fase', 'Um campo for atualizado', 'Um card for criado', 'Uma atividade for recorrente', 'Um alerta for acionado', 'Um card sair de uma fase', 'Um email for recebido', 'Todos os cards conectados forem movidos para uma fase', 'Uma resposta for recebida da automação de requisição HTTP', 'Um botão em Interfaces é clicado'. Actions: 'Peça à IA', 'Envie uma tarefa', 'Mova um card', 'Atualize um campo no card ou registro', 'Crie um card ou registro conectado', 'Crie um card ou registro', 'Mova o card pai', 'Distribua responsáveis', 'Aplique uma fórmula', 'Faça uma requisição HTTP', 'Aplique regras de SLA', and 'Envie um template de email' (rendered greyed-out/disabled in this trial org — likely plan-gated). Selecting a trigger opens an inline config card (e.g. 'Um card entrar em uma fase' → pipe selector locked to current pipe + 'Para a fase' dropdown + '+ Adicionar condição'). Selecting an action opens its own inline config card (e.g. 'Atualize um campo no card ou registro' → 'Onde está o campo' radio [Pipe atual / Pipe ou database conectado] → warning banner about validating required-field references → 'Selecione um campo' dropdown → a value input with a '+' token-picker button). The token picker is a searchable dropdown grouped into 'Atributos de evento' (e.g. Data e Hora do evento), 'Atributos gerais' (Criado em, Fase atual, Data de vencimento, Finalizado em, ID, A última fase em que o card estava, Título), then one group PER PHASE NAME (e.g. 'Start form', 'Caixa de entrada') each listing that phase's own fields — inserted tokens render as removable pills. Saving prompts for a rule name via a small modal, then the rule appears in the list with an enabled toggle. Screenshot: screenshots/inspect/automations-builder.jpg.
behavior: CONFIRMED end-to-end: created a rule (trigger: card enters phase 'Fazendo' in this pipe; action: update the 'Caixa de entrada' phase's 'Nome do solicitante' field, value = a token for the start form's 'Nome do solicitante' field). Dragged a real card into 'Fazendo' — a toast confirmed the move, then Automações > Logs showed a new row (automation name, card name, card id, status 'Sucesso', start timestamp) within seconds, expandable to 'Automação executada com sucesso.' Opening the card's detail view and expanding its 'Caixa de entrada' Histórico entry confirmed the target field's value was actually written (previously blank, now 'João Silva'). KEY FINDING: the action's target field is NOT restricted to the trigger's destination phase — 'Fazendo' has zero fields configured, yet the rule successfully wrote to a field on a different phase entirely ('Caixa de entrada'). This means automation actions must be modeled as free field references across the whole pipe (any phase/start-form field, keyed by field id), not scoped to the triggering phase. The value-editor's token picker confirms the same 'fields grouped by owner phase, independent rows even when labels collide' modeling already required by feature-004's card fields. Not yet tested: the other 9 trigger types or 11 action types (email-received, recurring-activity, HTTP round-trip, formula, SLA-rule actions) — only the phase-enter → update-field pair was exercised this pass.
data_model: automations: id, pipe_id (fk), name, enabled (bool), trigger_type (enum, 10 values), trigger_config (jsonb — e.g. {phaseId, conditions[]}), action_type (enum, 12 values), action_config (jsonb — e.g. {targetFieldId, targetFieldOwnerId, value: string with embedded {{token}} refs}), created_at, updated_at, updated_by_user_id. automation_runs: id, automation_id (fk), card_id (fk), card_title (denormalized for the log list), status (enum: success|error), message (text), started_at.

description: Field Conditionals — rule engine that shows/hides (and otherwise acts on) phase fields based on other field values
ui_details: Button in the Fases editor's top-right opens a 'Condicionais de campo' panel: search box, 'Campo: Todos'/'Uso do campo: Todos' filters, a banner explaining 'As condicionais agora estão em uma única lista, e são processadas de cima para baixo. Em caso de conflito, a última prevalece' (conditionals are a single ordered list, processed top-to-bottom, last one wins on conflict), a scrollable list of existing conditionals (each rendered as a small card: trigger condition → 'Então faça isso' action), and a 'Criar condicional' button. The builder modal ('Criar condicional'): 'Nome da condicional' text input, 'Defina as condições' (a 'Selecione um campo' dropdown + 'Adicionar condição' to AND more field checks + 'Novo grupo de condições' to add an OR'd group), then two action sections — 'Quando as condições forem verdadeiras' (Ação dropdown, default 'Ocultar' [hide], + target field dropdown + 'Adicionar ação') and 'Quando as condições forem falsas' (same shape, mirrored action for the false branch).
behavior: Not yet tested end-to-end (no conditional was saved during this pass — cancelled out of the builder after inspecting its shape). Confirmed structurally: conditionals are pipe-phase-scoped, ordered (array, not a set — order determines conflict resolution), each has a condition tree (AND within a group via 'Adicionar condição', OR across groups via 'Novo grupo de condições') and two action lists (true-branch, false-branch), where each action is at least {action: 'Ocultar'|..., targetFieldId}. Only 'Ocultar' was observed as a default action value — other action verbs (e.g. show/require) were not enumerated this pass; verify the full action-type list in a follow-up iteration by opening the action dropdown.
data_model: field_conditionals: id, phase_id (fk), name, position (int, determines evaluation/conflict order), condition_groups (jsonb — array of AND-groups, each an array of {field_id, operator, value}), true_actions (jsonb array of {action, target_field_id}), false_actions (jsonb array of {action, target_field_id})

unit.name: conditionals evaluate in position order with last-write-wins on conflict
unit.description: If two conditionals target the same field with contradictory actions, the one with the higher position (later in the list) determines the final state
unit.input: evaluateConditionals(cardFieldValues) with conditional A (position 0, hides field X) and conditional B (position 1, shows field X), both triggered
unit.expected_output: field X ends up visible (B, the later one, wins)

unit.name: AND within a condition group, OR across groups
unit.description: A conditional with two groups — group 1: [fieldA=1 AND fieldB=2], group 2: [fieldC=3] — triggers if either group fully matches
unit.input: cardFieldValues where fieldC=3 but fieldA/fieldB don't match group 1
unit.expected_output: conditional triggers (group 2 alone satisfies the OR)

e2e.name: create a conditional that hides a field
steps: Open Gerenciar > Fases > Condicionais em campos > Criar condicional
Name it 'Hide priority unless approved'
Set condition: 'Status' field equals 'Pendente'
Under 'Quando as condições forem verdadeiras', leave Ação as 'Ocultar' and target the 'Prioridade' field
Save
e2e.expected: Conditional appears in the list; on a card's field-fill form, setting Status to 'Pendente' hides the Prioridade field

edge_cases.name: conditional references a field that gets deleted
steps: Create a conditional targeting field X
Delete field X from the phase
edge_cases.expected: Either the conditional is auto-removed/disabled, or it's flagged as broken — verify against real UI in a follow-up pass
